as_told.title: Giza as the floor of the Tethys Sea with hydrothermal vents

plain: The ground the Giza pyramids stand on, the story goes, was once the floor of an ancient ocean called the Tethys Sea, millions of years ago. The researcher Geoffrey Drumm (also listed as Jeffrey Drum) says this in two separate episodes. He adds that vertical columns showing up in radar scans beneath the site, made by the team of a scientist named Filippo Biondi using satellite radar, "could be the remnants of some of these hydrothermal mineral vents," meaning hot mineral springs on the old seabed, with a magma chamber below them. If true, it would give the site a natural source of the chemicals his pyramid theory needs.
